question: Should ClawHub standardize a skill capability manifest now, and what schema, authority model, and rollout policy should be approved?
rationale: The next step changes the skill trust boundary and security review contract, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent schema or enforcement posture.

options.title: Spec first, advisory rollout
options.body: Approve a versioned manifest contract in specs/docs, ship advisory declared-vs-observed review output first, and defer required enforcement until scanner and legacy behavior are calibrated.

options.title: Defer manifest contract
options.body: Keep using ClawScan purpose-capability review and existing env/dependency declarations until adjacent RFCs settle the broader security-review model.

options.title: Revive prior implementation
options.body: Use the closed capability-manifest PR as a starting branch, but require fixes for the maintainer-identified parsing/API and rollout problems before merge.

recommendation.title: Spec first, advisory rollout
recommendation.body: Approve a versioned manifest contract in specs/docs, ship advisory declared-vs-observed review output first, and defer required enforcement until scanner and legacy behavior are calibrated.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS and blame connect this handle to the schema, moderation, and scan-enforcement surfaces that would define the trust-boundary contract.
